extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in anabelian/arithmetic geometry and readers of Mochizuki/IUT-related work
extracted.subtask_description: Group-theoretic reconstruction of arithmetic/geometric data (decomposition/inertia groups, cyclotomes, function field, constant field) of hyperbolic orbicurves and local fields from profinite fundamental-group extensions; includes cyclotomic rigidity statements and Kummer/cohomological characterisations used in the algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic Rigidity for Inertia Subgroups (Proposition 3.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume X has genus >= 2, Xbar its smooth compactification, U a non-empty open subscheme. For x in X(k) \ U(k) let Ix be the inertia subgroup of x in π1(U). There is a canonical (group-theoretically reconstructed) isomorphism (Cyc. Rig. Iner.) bZ(1)_X ≃ Ix arising from cohomology (Leray spectral sequence) and sending 1 ∈ bZ to the natural generator of Ix; kernels of maps π1(U) -> π1(U_x) are generated by inertia subgroups of U_x ∩ U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement is obtained via the exact sequence 1→Ix→π1^cusp-cent(U_x)→π1(X)→1 and the Leray spectral sequence; the isomorphism identifies the 'bZ(1)' coming from H^2 with the inertia cyclotome. It is used to remove bZ(2)-indeterminacy on cyclotomes when reconstructing local inertia data purely group-theoretically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial cyclotomic rigidity via finite étale covers (Remark 3.14.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X may not have genus ≥2, take a finite étale cover Y→X with genus ≥2 and a point y over x; the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism for Y induces a canonical isomorphism bZ(1)_X → Ix independent (functorially) of the choice of cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a method to extend cyclotomic rigidity to curves of lower genus by descent through finite étale covers; commutative diagrams show functorial compatibility across multiple covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of sections t_x and t_D via Picard schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: For a proper hyperbolic curve X, the natural map X→J^1 (Picard J^1) induces on fundamental groups sections t_x: G_k → π1(J^1). For a divisor D of degree d with support in X(k), linear combinations of t_x give t_D: G_k → π1(J^d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sections produce cocycles whose Kummer classes in H^1(G_k, π1(J)) are used to detect principal divisors and to relate arithmetic points/divisors to cohomology classes in the reconstruction process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer map injectivity and cohomological identifications (Lemma 3.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume k is Kummer-faithful and X proper. For nonempty open U⊂X the Kummer composite map O(U)× → H^1(π1(U), bZ(π1(X))) is injective. Also: (2) a section t_D equals the origin-section iff D is principal; (3) for U=X\S with S⊂X(k) finite, the quotient π1^cusp-cent(U) induces an isomorphism on H^1 with bZ(π1(X)); (4) H^1(π1(X), bZ(π1(X))) ≅ (k×)^; (5) restriction to inertia at S yields an exact sequence identifying H^1(π1^cusp-cent(U); bZ(π1(X))) with (k×)^ plus direct sum of bZ's over S; (6) image of principal divisors with support in S corresponds to specified submodule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These points give the cohomological dictionary between principal divisors/Kummer classes, H^1 of fundamental groups with cyclotome coefficients, and the profinite completion of k×. They are used to characterise principal cuspidal divisors group-theoretically.

rubrics_metrics.name: General anabelian methodology principle (Remark 3.15.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-step methodology: (1) Study objects in scheme theory to obtain group-theoretic properties/characterisations; (2) Use those group-theoretic properties to formulate purely group-theoretic reconstruction algorithms where scheme theory cannot be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why one first uses geometric/scheme-theoretic arguments to find invariants, then translates them into group-theoretic algorithms; highlights bZ(2)-torsor indeterminacy for cyclotomes absent cyclotomic rigidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation of Kummer classes of NF-rational functions and NF-constants (Lemma 3.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let U be an NF-curve (X defined over k_NF) and PU the inverse image of principal cuspidal divisors in H^1(π1(U); bZ(π1(X))). (1) An element α∈PU is the Kummer class of a non-constant NF-rational function iff some multiple n·α restricts at two NF-points x1,x2 (over a finite extension k0) to sections s_{x_i} with (n·α)|_{x1}=0, (n·α)|_{x2}≠0. (2) If non-constant NF-rational functions exist, α∈PU ∩ H^1(G_k; bZ(π1(X))) = (k×)^ is the Kummer class of an NF-constant iff there exist an NF-rational f and an NF-point x with (Kummer map of f)|_x = α|_x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives cohomological criteria (via restriction to decomposition groups/points) to decide when a cohomology class arises from a rational function or a constant, used in the reconstruction algorithm to detect function-field elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-anabelian Reconstruction of NF-Portion (Theorem 3.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume k is sub-p-adic, X a hyperbolic orbicurve of strictly Belyi type. From the extension 1→π1(X)→π1^geom(X)→G_k→1 we can functorially reconstruct the NF-rational function field k_NF(X) and the NF-constant field k_NF purely group-theoretically. The theorem outlines a five-step reconstruction: (1) Belyi cuspidalisation reconstructs surjections π1(U)→π1(X) and decomposition/inertia groups; (2) cyclotomic rigidity recovers canonical identifications Ix ≃ bZ(1)_X; (3) reconstruct restrictions H^1(π1(U); bZ(π1(X)))→H^1(Ix; bZ(π1(X))) and the exact sequence identifying (k×)^; (4) characterise NF-rational functions and constants in PU and reconstruct subgroups via Kummer maps; (5) apply Uchida's lemma to recover additive structures and hence k_NF(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The steps are constructive and functorial for open injective homomorphisms of profinite group-extensions and base-change; cyclotomic rigidity is essential to avoid bZ(2)-indeterminacy. The theorem provides the core algorithm for recovering arithmetic data from group data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input-data minimisation for number/local fields (Remark 3.17.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is a number field or a non-Archimedean local field, one needs only the profinite group π1^geom(X) (i.e., π1(X)) as input to the reconstruction by Proposition 2.2(1) and Corollary 2.4, because cuspidal decomposition groups are group-theoretically characterised in these cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: in arithmetic applications the full extension by G_k may not be necessary; reconstruction can be done from the profinite fundamental group alone under these base-field hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary birational analogue (Remark 3.17.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is l-cyclotomically full for some l and k is Kummer-faithful, starting from the extension for the generic point 1→π1(η_X)→?→G_k→1 (rather than for X) the algorithm reconstructs k(X) and k (not only NF-portions) without Belyi cuspidalisation or (GC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows a stronger birational reconstruction is possible under cyclotomic fullness and Kummer-faithfulness; avoids reliance on cuspidalisation or global conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomes of G_k and their functoriality (Definition 3.18 and Remark 3.18.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For k a finite extension of Q_p define Q/Z(G_k):= lim_{G_k':open} H_ab(G_k')_tors (transition by transfer) and bZ(G_k):=Hom(Q/Z, Q/Z(G_k)). These 'cyclotomes' are used in cohomology; for open injective homomorphisms of profinite groups the maps between cyclotomes multiply by the index [G_k:G_k'] on cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the formal definition of cyclotomic coefficient modules attached to G_k and records the scaling behaviour under open subgroups (important for functoriality in reconstruction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-anabelian Reconstruction over a non-Archimedean local field (Corollary 3.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume k is a non-Archimedean local field and X a hyperbolic orbicurve of strictly Belyi type. From the profinite group π1^geom(X) one can reconstruct functorially: (1) the set of decomposition groups of all closed points of X; (2) the function field k(X) and constant field k; (3) a natural cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (Cyc. Rig. LCFT) bZ(G_k) ≃ bZ(O((π1^geom(X)))) (classical cyclotomic rigidity via local class field theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses Theorem 3.17 and group-theoretic constructions of H^2(G_k; bZ(G_k)) and cup-products; the isomorphism is compatible with the previously reconstructed isomorphisms and uses LCFT to relate global cyclotomes to local ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity via LCFT for monoids/groups and Kummer isomorphism (Remark 3.19.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a topological monoid/group M with continuous G_k-action and isomorphic to O((π1^geom(X))) as G_k-module, define bZ(M):=Hom(Q/Z, M^ab) etc. Then H^2(G_k; bZ(Q/Z(M))) identifies with H^2(Gur; Z) leading to canonical Cyclotomic Rigidity isomorphisms (Cyc. Rig. LCFT2) bZ(G_k) ≃ bZ(M) and canonical homomorphisms M → lim_{J:open} H^1(J; bZ(M)). In the O-case these induce Kummer isomorphisms Kum: M ⊗ Q ≃ O_k((π1^geom(X))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalises LCFT-cyclotomic rigidity to other topological monoids/groups M with G_k-action and gives canonical injections/isomorphisms used to incorporate value-group (O) data into reconstruction algorithms; notes potential ±1 indeterminacy in choices of generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy of arithmetic holomorphicity and mono-analyticity
rubrics_metrics.description: View non-scheme-theoretic automorphisms of G_k as 'arithmetically holomorphic' (image via scheme-to-group map) and treat the right-hand group-theoretic side as 'mono-analytic'. Multiplicative structures (k×) and unramified quotient (value group) are inter-universally rigid (reconstructible from G_k), while additive structures and inertia/unit group filtrations are inter-universally non-rigid (exist non-scheme automorphisms of G_k that do not preserve ramification filtrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conceptual principle explains which pieces of a local/global field are rigid under abstract profinite-group automorphisms and motivates why reconstruction algorithms need to 'rigidify' certain portions (e.g., via cyclotomic data) to recover additive information; references to results showing rigidity after imposing ramification-preserving conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical note on reconstruction without strictly Belyi type (Remark 3.19.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if X is not strictly Belyi type one can construct a cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism bZ(G_k) ≃ bZ(π1^geom(X)), but this requires longer reconstruction algorithms involving graphs of special fibres and Raynaud theory; avoids using pGC but is more technical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that the strictly Belyi hypothesis simplifies reconstruction; without it one must reconstruct additional tempered/rational positive structures and use deep results about Jacobians and special fibres.
